title: Older musicians: Willie Parker, Landry and Rodgers
summary: Interviewer asks about old players Willie Parker, Al Landry, Ernest Rodgers, and places they played.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You know, I guess Willie Parker's about the oldest musician living. You know him? Remember him? He's a bass drum player and clarinet player? Who they? Willie Parker. He's still alive. Boy, he's an old man. He played with the Lions Brass Band. The Terminal Brass Band. He's doing some bands. I don't know. You didn't know that? I don't know. I can't.
I can't. Man Creole and She-Cole. That was before the 20's. He with Pico?
With Pico? I say with a guy called Man Creole and She-Cole. That was before the 20's. He with Pico?
With Pico? With a guy called Man Creole and She-Cole. I think She-Cole played baritone on one. I don't know them.
I think he got some fellas way back there, man.
Oh, Al Landry and Ernest Rogers, I think he worked with them. Some.
I know Landry. Big old red. I think Rodgers. I know him. Big old Landry. Yeah. Did you ever work with Landry?
He played with the, he used to play with the Ricker.
Oh yeah, Landry. He used to play with. He used to play down at Lutton's. Do you remember the Bern, that place?

You read about that in the paper? No. He played at Lutton's. Landry played that with Big Al Louie. You call it the old folks home, it's down on Almanaster. Oh, they had that place there for years. Billy and the Dee and George Lewis. All those. Used to be like that. Well, I guess you all have been away from New Orleans too long. No, I didn't get back.
But Lord, every place when I was there, I didn't know nothing about who.
